newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila stocks end up for 6th straight session.
newsitem.headline: Manila stocks end up for 6th straight session.

text.p: * Main index a shade lower the 3,000-barrier
Bargain hunting on select issues in late trade lifted Manila stocks for the sixth consecutive session on Wednesday, brokers said.
"The market trekked cautiously as local and foreign investors took their time buying and selling in between trades," said Monique Lecaros at Armstrong Securities.
The main index was up 11.25 points to 2,998.43.
Brokers said government reports of a lower-than-expected October inflation helped build confidence in the local market.
"Foreign investors though are a bit cautious while waiting for the elections result in the United States," Lecaros said.

"A Clinton win will have an indirect effect on the Philippine market," said Fitz Aclan, research head of Dharmala Securities, adding that the re-election of the current U.S. President is expected to prop up the Dow Jones.
Some 8.5 billion shares worth 2.59 billion pesos changed hands in range-bound trade.
